_about: Standalone cases shown in the Case library on the HQ screen, in this order. Add one with: ./sentinel case publish ID --library --teaser "..."

cases.teaser: A dental group's staff intranet server did something at half past one in the morning. Their IT manager says the portal is internal-only and it was probably a maintenance job.
A housing charity's SIEM caught something on a server that appeared and vanished almost instantly, just after midnight. Their IT team says their patch tool does that all the time.
A receptionist at a vet practice followed an online guide to fix the label printer. She says she ran one command, nothing happened, and then she rang IT.
A print shop's design workstation ran a Windows utility with a web address attached. The owner says the user has no admin rights, so nothing could have been installed.
A credit union's domain controller ran a command as SYSTEM in the middle of the afternoon. Their sysadmin checked straight away: nobody was logged on.
Someone cleared the Security log on a food distributor's server during the evening. The client says it was an admin tidying up, and you've been sent the next few seconds of events.
A paralegal's workstation started running commands well after she'd gone home. The firm's sysadmin says their inventory tool sometimes trips the alarm in the evenings.
